Etsu Inagaki Sugimoto, A Daughter of the Samurai.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/etsu-inagaki-sugimoto/a-daughter-of-the-samurai

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Etsu Inagaki Sugimoto, the author, died 1950 (Wikidata Q2363769, P570 = 1950-06-20 in the facts file).
- Christopher Morley, the writer of the introduction, died 1957 (Wikidata Q931105, P570 = 1957-03-28).

First publication of the text used: 1925 (SE colophon: 'A Daughter of the Samurai was published in 1925 by Etsu Inagaki Sugimoto.'). Wikipedia: serialized in the US magazine Asia, then published as a book in 1925 by Doubleday; the article notes that some sources date the book to 1926.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition states the text is in the United States public domain (statement quoted below), and the text was first published in the United States in 1925, before 1931.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published in the United States, before 1931, so the US rule settles the country of origin whatever the death years. Sugimoto died in 1950 and Morley in 1957; neither date changes the result.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: published 1925 by Etsu Inagaki Sugimoto.
- Wikipedia, A Daughter of the Samurai: serialized in the magazine Asia, released as a book in 1925 by Doubleday. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Daughter_of_the_Samurai
- Wikidata Q2363769 (Etsu Inagaki Sugimoto), P570 = 1950-06-20 in the facts file; Wikidata Q931105 (Christopher Morley), P570 = 1957-03-28
